items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The section banners and Chinese comments help, but business logic uses single-letter and cryptic names throughout: `S`, `p`, `v`, `q`, `r`, `l`, `r2`, `nq`, `rf`, `df`, `T(...)`, `c2y`. Example: `var p = S.products.filter(...)[0], v = selectedVariant(p);`. The single-letter cap applies.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One 1667-line file (the >500-line cap applies). The ops layer (`opAddToCart`, `opCheckout`, `computeStats`) is separated from the UI, but `bind()` holds one large switch that mixes inline business logic (`S.cart = []; S.couponCode = null`) with UI handling. `api.reset` duplicates the UI checkout-state reset.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: `txn()` rolls back failed operations, and the code handles corrupt storage and missing localStorage. However, `try { renderAll(); } catch (e) { /* 渲染问题不影响业务结果 */ }` silently swallows errors. There are magic numbers (9.5折, thresholds). The hidden test `test_coupon_threshold_and_invalidation` failed: an unmet coupon stays selected.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: The cart shows a breakdown and a rules box covering stacking order and threshold. Status tags and flow appear, and only the allowed actions are shown for each status. `confirmDanger` covers cancel, refund, restock, import, reset, clear cart, and removal. Toasts and field errors use plain Chinese.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The API wraps the same `opX` functions through `apiRun(txn(...))`. Money is in cents (e.g. `amount: 7349`, converted with `c2y`). `getStats` calls `computeStats(S.orders)` every time. Import goes through `opImport` inside `txn`, so a failure leaves data unchanged.
